medications.reason: Psychosis on dopamine agonist; taper off over two weeks

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Movement disorders clinic

Dear Doctor,

I saw Roger Desrosiers, 69, today with his wife, about nine months after our April visit for visual hallucinations. Thank you for your call in December.

His wife reports two months of visual hallucinations and paranoid thinking. He again sees small animals in the house, which she confirms are not there, and he has become suspicious of the neighbors, accusing them of taking things from him with nothing to support it. These began after pramipexole was added in October, three months ago. He takes carbidopa-levodopa, pramipexole, atorvastatin and metoprolol among his medicines. He has never had psychiatric illness.

BP 130/80, HR 68, afebrile.
Exam: rest tremor, bradykinesia and rigidity as before. No signs of infection or a metabolic cause on exam. MMSE 26/30, points lost on attention and calculation.

Assessment: psychosis induced by dopaminergic therapy, specifically the dopamine agonist, in a patient with Parkinson disease psychosis and mild cognitive impairment.

Plan:
1. Taper pramipexole off over two weeks: 0.125 mg three times daily for one week, then 0.125 mg twice daily for one week, then stop.
2. Continue carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily and rasagiline 1 mg daily.
3. Wife to call us if symptoms worsen during the taper. Follow-up in two months.

Movement disorders neurologist

documents.title: Check-in call

documents.body: Called wife per PCP to check on taper. Last pramipexole dose was yesterday. She thinks he is calmer and has stopped talking about the neighbors this week. Still sees an animal occasionally. No falls, sleeping ok. Has neuro f/u in March and AWV with us next month.

Functional: needs a little more help with the pill box now, wife fills it. Still independent for ADLs. No falls.

Exam: per flowsheet. Alert, oriented, conversant. Masking, R tremor, mild bradykinesia. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.

Plan:
- Psychosis improving off agonist, neuro f/u 3/13.
- MCI: per neuro, wife managing meds, good.
- HTN/HLD: labs today.
- Vaccines up to date.
- RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology

Movement disorders clinic

Mr. Desrosiers returns with his wife two months after we stopped pramipexole. The paranoid ideas about the neighbors are gone and the visual hallucinations have resolved; his wife has not heard him mention the animals in several weeks. Motor function is similar to before the agonist trial.

Exam: rest tremor right hand, bradykinesia, rigidity right greater than left, unchanged.

Assessment: dopamine agonist induced psychosis, resolved after withdrawal. Parkinson disease with prior psychosis and mild cognitive impairment.
Plan: no dopamine agonists going forward. Continue carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily and rasagiline 1 mg daily. Follow-up in six months.

Movement disorders neurologist

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 01/08/2024. Received 01/11/2024.

CC: chest pain.

HPI: 70M with Parkinson disease, HTN and hyperlipidemia, here with two hours of central chest pressure that started while shoveling snow from his driveway. Pain goes into the left arm, with shortness of breath. Denies nausea, vomiting or sweating. Stopped shoveling, pain eased but did not go away.

PMH: Parkinson disease with prior medication-related psychosis, mild cognitive impairment, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH, diverticulosis with diverticular bleed 2021.
Meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate, carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, tamsulosin, finasteride.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Retired teacher. Lives with wife.
FH: father MI at 72.

Triage: BP 150/90, HR 85, RR 18, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: mildly pale, otherwise unremarkable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Rest tremor right hand.

ECG: sinus, no ST elevation, T-wave inversions V4-V6.
Labs: troponin I 0.08 ng/mL (ref <0.04). CK-MB 10 U/L (ref 0-5). Myoglobin 90 ng/mL (ref 28-72). CBC and BMP unremarkable.

ED course: aspirin 324 mg chewed, sublingual nitroglycerin with relief, heparin infusion started. Cardiology consulted, admitted to cardiology for catheterization.

Impression: NSTEMI.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Procedure: left heart catheterization, coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention. Access: right radial artery, 6 Fr. Left main: no disease. LAD: culprit stenosis in the mid segment. Circumflex: no lesion requiring treatment. RCA: dominant, no lesion requiring treatment. Intervention: mid LAD treated with one drug-eluting stent, good angiographic result with brisk flow. Radial band applied, hemostasis.
reports.conclusion: Single-vessel coronary disease. Mid LAD culprit lesion treated with one drug-eluting stent. Dual antiplatelet therapy for at least 12 months.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 55%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV systolic function, LVEF 55%, no regional wall motion abnormality.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admission 01/08/2024 - Discharge 01/10/2024. Received 01/11/2024.

Discharge diagnoses: NSTEMI; coronary artery disease, single vessel, s/p drug-eluting stent to mid LAD.

Course: 70M with Parkinson disease, HTN, hyperlipidemia and prior diverticular bleed presented with exertional chest pressure while shoveling snow. Troponin I 0.08 with lateral T-wave inversions. Treated with aspirin, heparin and nitroglycerin; pain free by evening. Catheterization 1/9 via right radial: mid LAD culprit lesion, one DES placed; no other lesions needing treatment. Echo LVEF 55%, normal wall motion. No arrhythmia on telemetry. Radial site clean.

New medications:
- clopidogrel 75 mg daily, with aspirin, for at least 12 months. Do not stop without talking to cardiology.
- pantoprazole 40 mg daily for GI protection on dual antiplatelet therapy given the 2021 diverticular bleed.
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed.
Continued: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg, tamsulosin 0.4, finasteride 5.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Cardiology clinic in 4-5 weeks; cardiac rehab referral at that visit. No shoveling or heavy lifting for now.

Cardiology

documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, spoke with pt and wife. Home 1/10 after NSTEMI and LAD stent. No chest pain since, has not used the nitro. Right wrist mildly sore, no swelling. Picked up clopidogrel, pantoprazole, nitro. Wife set up the pill box with the new meds; reviewed not to skip clopidogrel. Appt with PCP 1/16 confirmed.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after NSTEMI. ED record, cath and echo reports, discharge summary reviewed.

1/8 chest pressure shoveling snow, troponin 0.08, TWI V4-V6. Cath 1/9: mid LAD culprit, 1 DES. EF 55%. Home 1/10.
Since: no chest pain, no nitro use, walking in the house and to the mailbox. No dyspnea, no palpitations. No bleeding, stools brown. Wrist fine.
Meds reconciled with wife: added clopidogrel 75, pantoprazole 40, NTG SL prn. Everything else unchanged.

Exam: BP and HR ok. R radial site healed, pulse 2+. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. NSTEMI s/p DES to LAD, CAD - DAPT at least 12 months, cardiology f/u in Feb with rehab referral. Reviewed chest pain plan and NTG use. No shoveling - neighbor's son is doing the driveway.
2. Bleeding risk on DAPT with prior diverticular bleed - on PPI; reviewed what to watch for.
3. HTN - ok on lisinopril/metoprolol.
4. HLD - atorvastatin 40 continued.
BMP, CBC today. RTC after cardiology.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Desrosiers is seen five weeks after NSTEMI treated with a drug-eluting stent to the mid LAD. He has had no chest pain, has not used nitroglycerin and is walking daily indoors. No bleeding on aspirin and clopidogrel.

Exam: BP and heart rate at goal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Right radial pulse normal. No edema.

Assessment: CAD s/p NSTEMI and LAD DES, LVEF 55%. Doing well.
Plan:
- Aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg for at least 12 months; pantoprazole continues.
- Continue metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40.
- Referral to cardiac rehabilitation, three sessions a week.
- Return in six months.

Cardiology

documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 06/27/2024. Received 07/01/2024.

CC: chest pain, STEMI alert.

HPI: 70M with CAD s/p NSTEMI with LAD stent in January and Parkinson disease, brought by ambulance with heavy substernal chest pain that began about two hours ago while he was sitting at rest. Radiates to the right arm. Nauseated and sweating. On aspirin and clopidogrel, has not missed doses per wife.

PMH: CAD s/p NSTEMI/LAD DES 1/2024, Parkinson disease with prior psychosis, MCI, HTN, hyperlipidemia, BPH, diverticulosis with 2021 bleed.
Meds: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole, carbidopa-levodopa, rasagiline, tamsulosin, finasteride, NTG prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 18, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: in distress, diaphoretic. JVD present. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. No peripheral edema.

ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF.
Labs: troponin I 8.0 ng/mL (ref <0.04). CK-MB 50 U/L (ref 0-24). BNP 80 pg/mL (ref 0-100).

Course: STEMI activation on ECG. Heparin bolus. Nitroglycerin withheld given pressure. Small fluid bolus. To cath lab at 08:05.

Impression: acute inferior STEMI.

Emergency medicine attending

reports.text: Procedure: emergent coronary angiography and primary PCI. Access: right radial artery, 6 Fr. Left main: no disease. LAD: previously placed mid LAD stent patent. Circumflex: no lesion requiring treatment. RCA: dominant, acute occlusion of the proximal segment with thrombus, culprit. Intervention: proximal RCA treated with one drug-eluting stent with restoration of brisk flow.
reports.conclusion: Acute inferior STEMI from proximal RCA occlusion, treated with one drug-eluting stent. Patent LAD stent.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size. LVEF 50%. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall. Remaining segments contract normally. Right ventricle normal in size. Valves without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admission 06/27/2024 - Discharge 06/30/2024. Received 07/01/2024.

Discharge diagnoses: acute inferior STEMI, s/p primary PCI with drug-eluting stent to proximal RCA. CAD with prior NSTEMI and mid LAD stent (patent).

Course: 70M, six months after NSTEMI, with rest chest pain, inferior ST elevation and hypotension. Emergent catheterization: proximal RCA occlusion, one DES; LAD stent patent. Pressure recovered with fluids after reperfusion; no pressors. Echo 6/28: LVEF 50%, inferior hypokinesis. Telemetry without sustained arrhythmia. Metoprolol held the first day and resumed at home dose before discharge. Ambulating with PT, steady.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75 (continue for 12 months from this event), pantoprazole 40, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, NTG SL prn, carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, rasagiline 1 mg, tamsulosin 0.4, finasteride 5.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week; cardiology in 6 weeks.

Cardiology

6/27 rest chest pain, STE II/III/aVF, BP 90/60. Primary PCI proximal RCA, 1 DES; LAD stent patent. EF now 50% with inferior hypokinesis. Home 6/30.
Since: no chest pain. Up and about at home. No dyspnea lying flat, no leg swelling, no palpitations. No bleeding. No confusion per wife.
Meds reconciled - no changes from pre-admission list.

Exam: BP and HR ok. Alert. Radial site healed. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. No JVD. No edema.

A/P:
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA DES, second MI in 6 months. DAPT through June 2025 per cardiology. Cardiology 8/12. He doesn't want to repeat rehab right now, will reconsider at cardiology visit.
2. HTN/HLD - same meds.
BMP today. RTC in the fall.
